newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian bullion up as global trends improve.
newsitem.headline: Indian bullion up as global trends improve.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 5 rupees higher at 4,740 rupees against the previous close of 4,735 rupees but off 15 rupees against today's opening prices of 4,755 rupees per 10 gramme.

** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees higher at 55,500 rupees per piece against the previous close of 55,400 rupees. They opened higher today at 55,600 rupees but later on sluggish seasonal buying eroded early gains towards the close.

** Silver (.999) closed 60 rupees higher at 7,340 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,280 rupees on the back of fresh industrial and speculative buying following uptrend in the world market while inflow was at a low ebb.

Gold 24 carat closed 5 rupees higher at 4,740 rupees per 10 grammes against the previous close of 4,735 rupees but off 15 rupees against today's opening prices of 4,755 rupees per 10 grammes, dealers said.

Gold opened higher today on the back of overnight gains in the world market but lower than expected seasonal buying and fresh profit-taking trimmed major part of the early gains towards the close, they said.

Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees higher at 55,500 rupees per piece against the previous close of 55,400 rupees. They opened higher today at 55,600 rupees but later slid down on improved supplies.
Biscuit prices were up by 100 rupees each on Wednesday but were down 500 rupees on Tuesday.

Meanwhile silver (.999) closed 60 rupees higher at 7,340 rupees per kg up against the previous close of 7,280 rupees on the back of renewed industrial buying as well as an uptrend in the world market which triggered fresh speculative interest.
Silver was down by 25 rupees per kg on Wednesday. Limited inflow and shortage of ready stock kept market sentiments firm at the close of the session. (Conversion $1=35.88 rupees)
